Title: US bans BYD from air base in Japan over security concern
Article:
SEOUL: The US armed forces have banned Chinese carmaker BYD's electric vehicles from an air base in Japan over security concerns, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported on Friday, after Washington added the company to a list of enterprises it believes are aiding China's military.
The concern stems from the use of cameras and sensors mounted on the vehicles, which the US believes could collect and leak sensitive security-related information from the base, Yonhap reported, citing US military officials stationed in Japan.
US military officials in Japan could not immediately be reached for confirmation.
BYD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Kadena Air Base in Okinawa will turn away BYD cars starting on Monday, Yonhap reported. Vehicles used by base personnel, contractors, commercial entities and taxis will be affected without exception, the agency said.
In June, the US added BYD, e-commerce company Alibaba, internet company Baidu and automaker NIO to a list of companies it believes are aiding China's military.
Alibaba has since sued the US government. China's Foreign Ministry has protested that the list is discriminatory and unreasonable.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix AI misses D-Day on RM2bil sukuk breach, default risk looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd seems to have missed Thursday's deadline to resolve a covenant breach under its RM2 billion sukuk programme.
As of press time, Zetrix AI had not issued any statement on whether it had secured a waiver from sukukholders or reached an agreement with the sukuk trustee.
Without a resolution, the digital services and blockchain group faces potential repayment obligations of RM2.16 billion, comprising RM2 billion in principal and RM164.5 million in future coupon payments.
The breach arose after managing director Wong Thean Soon ceased to be the company's single largest shareholder following a series of forced share sales linked to margin calls on his share-backed financing facilities.
His combined direct and indirect shareholding fell from nearly 30 per cent to 1.895 per cent as at Oct 15, triggering a breach of the sukuk covenant requiring him to remain the company's largest shareholder.
As at the time of writing, Wong had not responded to Business Times for comment.
In its earlier filing with Bursa Malaysia, Zetrix AI said it would seek sukukholders' consent through an extraordinary resolution, including a possible waiver, if the breach remained unresolved by Oct 22.
Without a waiver, a dissolution event could be triggered, allowing the sukuk trustee to accelerate repayment of outstanding amounts.
However, the missed deadline does not in itself confirm that the trustee has demanded immediate repayment or that a payment default has occurred.
The development adds to pressure on the group, which recently withdrew its proposed interim dividend of 0.25 sen a share, citing the need to preserve working capital amid unexpected operational expenses.
Zetrix AI is also facing scrutiny over RM314 million in unremitted collections owed to the Road Transport Department.
MARC Ratings, meanwhile, has downgraded its sukuk rating to BB+IS from AA-IS and maintained a negative outlook, citing deterioration in its financial and liquidity position, governance concerns and heightened covenant risks.
The company's next move, and whether sukukholders will grant a waiver, remain key uncertainties for investors.

Title: Japan's core inflation exceeds BoJ target, cements near-term rate hike chance
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's two per cent target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike.
The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust artificial intelligence demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies.
Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, sources have told Reuters.
"Core inflation is expected to accelerate due to rising energy costs from the Middle East conflict and subsequent second-round effects," said Masato Koike, a senior economist at Sompo Institute Plus.
"But with price rises not accelerating sharply, there's little need for a back-to-back rate increase in October," he said, projecting the BoJ's next hike to come in December.
The core consumer price index, which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast and accelerating from a 1.7 per cent rise in August.
An index that strips away the effects of both volatile fresh food and fuel, which is closely watched by the BoJ as a better gauge of demand-driven price pressures, rose 2.4 per cent in September from a year earlier after increasing 1.9 per cent in August.
In a sign of broadening inflationary pressure, goods prices rose 2.8 per cent year-on-year in September, accelerating from a 2.6 per cent gain in August, the data showed.
Services inflation also accelerated to 1.5 per cent in September from 1.2 per cent in the previous month, suggesting firms were passing on higher labour costs from a tight job market.
RISK OF HIGHER TERMINAL RATE
The data will be among factors the BoJ will scrutinise in producing fresh quarterly growth and price forecasts at next week's two-day policy meeting ending on Oct 30.
Sources have told Reuters the BoJ may signal that underlying inflation - or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors - likely achieved two per cent, and stress its focus on anchoring inflation around the target.
Governor Kazuo Ueda said last week the BoJ won't tolerate any inflation overshoot, signalling resolve to continue raising rates after lifting them to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent last month.
Recent surveys showed few signs past rate hikes were cooling loan demand, suggesting scope for further rate increases and drawing attention to the BoJ's assessment on lending conditions.
Many analysts polled by Reuters expect the BoJ to raise its policy rate to 1.50 per cent in December, and predict the terminal rate to be around 1.75 per cent or two per cent.
Marcel Thieliant, head of Asia-Pacific at Capital Economics, projects the oJ to leave policy steady next week but signal continued concerns about upside risks to inflation.
"With little evidence that the tightening delivered so far has slowed the economy, the risks are shifting towards a higher peak in the policy rate than our forecast of two per cent," Thieliant said.

Title: Eight Thais held for running tomyam businesses on visit passes
Article:
BALIK PULAU: Eight Thai citizens were arrested for allegedly operating tomyam eateries using social visit passes and border passes during an integrated operation in Balik Pulau.
The operation was conducted by the Penang Immigration Department in collaboration with the  Penang Island City Council, the Companies Commission of Malaysia, and the Department of Labour following public complaints.
Penang Immigration director Syamsul Fitry Ahmad said the operation, which ended at 1am, targeted foreign-run businesses, particularly those operated by Thais.
"Checks led to the arrest of five men and three women, aged between 30 and 40, suspected of running businesses without valid passes or permits.
"Some of them were using social visit passes and border passes," he said.
The eight will be taken to the Jawi Immigration Depot for further investigation and action.
During the same operation, the local council seized all equipment from two premises.
Syamsul Fitry reminded business operators, particularly tomyam restaurant owners, to comply with procedures governing business operations and foreign worker recruitment.
"We have a special pass for tomyam business operators. Employers must ensure that the recruitment of workers complies with all established procedures," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail Lasim denies reports he will resign as Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has denied reports that he will resign soon to make way for someone else amid the ongoing constitutional crisis in the state.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, described the claim circulating on social media as merely "political games" by certain quarters.
"Just political games... It is not true. I am not resigning," he said briefly when contacted this morning.
Earlier, a Chinese-language portal reported that Ismail would sign a letter of resignation.
The report, headlined "Ismail Lasim has signed his resignation letter", also highlighted the ongoing administrative crisis involving the palace, which has yet to show signs of being resolved.
Ismail's press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, also denied the report, describing it as untrue.
"The menteri besar is carrying out his duties as usual. The report (claim) is untrue," he said.
Yesterday, Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias called on all parties to give the
state leadership
room to resolve the matter.
The former senior executive councillor under the Pakatan Harapan administration said there was no need for concern as the crisis was expected to be resolved soon.
On Sept 20, Istana Seri Menanti announced that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of 10 executive councillors appointed by Ismail.
The development came after Ismail was reported to have signed a proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz from the throne on Aug 3, a day after he was sworn in as Menteri Besar.
Ismail also came under the spotlight after Tuanku Muhriz
openly reprimanded him
following Friday prayers at Masjid Kampung Beting, Juasseh, Kuala Pilah, last week.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aunty Elen's story highlights the strength of Malaysia's neighbourly ties [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: For longtime Duyong resident Aunty Elen, decades of friendship with neighbours of different races have grown into close bonds built on shared experiences, trust and mutual support.
Duyong assemblyman Mohd Noor Helmy shared her story in a video posted on social media.
In the video, Aunty Elen recalls fond memories with her friends, from sharing meals and secrets to making up after disagreements.
"I have been here for a long time. I moved here when I got married 50 years ago," she said, recounting her years in the area.
She spoke warmly of the close ties she shared with her friends, who stood by one another through the ups and downs of everyday life.
"We can argue, but after that, we make up. Sometimes she cries for me, and I cry for her," she said.
Noor Helmy said he had known Aunty Elen as a longtime resident in his constituency and had visited her home after a flood to help resolve a drainage issue.
He added that he often saw her spending time with other residents whenever he visited the area.
He said he shared her story as an example of the close bonds that could develop between people of different races.
"Today, we acknowledge that Malays, Chinese and Indians have no problem being friends. But a deeper bond, a friendship like that between siblings, is something we rarely see," he said.
He said community ties could be strengthened through neighbourhood interactions, business dealings and shared interests.
Neighbours, he added, were often among the first to offer help when someone faced difficulties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Islamic preacher Ustaz Wadi Annuar believed among victims in Gerik three-vehicle crash
Article:
GERIK: Islamic preacher Ustaz Wadi Annuar is believed to have been among the occupants of a Toyota Vellfire involved in a three-vehicle crash along the East-West Highway near Gerik early today.
The 2.40am accident involved a Perodua Myvi, a Toyota Vellfire, and a Perodua Bezza, leaving five people injured, while five others escaped unhurt.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call via the NG999 system before dispatching a team from the Gerik station to the scene.
"The team arrived at 3.42am, about 59km from the station, and found that the Myvi had veered off the road into a drain.
"A 25-year-old man was trapped in the front passenger seat of the car, while its 24-year-old driver sustained serious injuries," he said.
He said another 24-year-old male passenger seated at the rear suffered minor injuries.
"Four occupants of the Vellfire, comprising two injured and two uninjured victims, had been extricated by members of the public before the fire and rescue team arrived.
"The Myvi driver and two injured occupants of the Vellfire had also been taken to Gerik Hospital by Health Ministry ambulances before the team arrived," he said.
He said the three occupants of the Bezza were unhurt, but the vehicle was no longer at the scene as its owner had gone to a police station to lodge a report.
"The operation commander conducted an assessment before directing personnel to use rescue equipment to free the trapped victim, who was found to have sustained serious injuries.
"Two victims from the Myvi were taken to Gerik Hospital using the department's Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicle for further treatment," he said.
He added the operation was brought under control at 4.10am and ended at 4.39am, involving 10 personnel and three vehicles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher as AI investment concerns weigh on greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher on Friday as the greenback weakened after equity prices fell amid heightened concern over artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0785/0855 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0815/0850.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the concerns stemmed from investors' doubts over whether further investments in AI-related companies would generate returns in a timely manner.
He also said the possibility of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed) is diminishing as two- and 10-year US Treasury yields fell by 16 and 17 basis points to 4.64 per cent and 4.95 per cent, respectively.
Mohd Afzanizam added that the US Dollar Index eased 0.15 per cent to 101.625 points.
"However, there is growing concern about growth prospects, making the rate hike decision appear to be unrealistic. As such, ringgit would likely maintain its narrow range trade today as market sentiments look defensive," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies at the opening.
It edged up vis-a-vis the euro to 4.5765/5843 from 4.5790/5830, but eased versus the Japanese yen to 2.6054/6100 from 2.6035/6057 at Thursday's close and inched down against the British pound to 5.4664/4758 from 5.4659/4706.
Meanwhile, the ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It gained versus the Thai baht to 12.0852/1124 from 12.0973/1120 at yesterday's close, and rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.8/226.3 from 225.9/226.3. The ringgit was flat vis-a-vis the Philippine peso at 6.42/6.43.
The ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1941/1998 from 3.1917/1947 at Thursday's close.

Title: #NSTviral: Man cradling two baby crocodiles fascinates netizens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two baby crocodiles, an unusual lullaby and a man rocking the reptiles to sleep — hardly an everyday naptime scene.
That was what greeted Threads users in a viral video posted by bedamau_bro, showing a man cradling one crocodile in his arms while another rested on his lap at an amusement park in Selayang.
The clip has garnered more than 15,000 likes, with netizens fascinated by the unusual encounter.
The reptiles even have names — Ali and Ahcong — as the user revealed in the comments while inviting visitors to meet them.
He also offered visitors the chance to hold either crocodile or take photographs with them at the park.
While the reptiles may look cute at this size, crocodiles are wild animals and should not be handled without expert supervision.
The saltwater crocodile, which is found naturally in Malaysia, is the world's largest living crocodilian and is known to attack humans. However, the video did not identify the species of Ali and Ahcong.

Title: Oil tanker rate spike: Gains for some, pain for others [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Surging oil tanker rates amid the Middle East conflict could raise operating costs for Malaysia's oil and gas (O&G) industry, although economists said upstream producers and tanker operators may benefit from higher crude prices and charter rates.
Oil tanker rates for very large crude carriers (VLCC) from the Persian Gulf to Asia climbed to more than US$37 per barrel by mid-October, more than five times their pre-conflict levels, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Wednesday.
The agency attributed the surge to congestion in the Strait of Hormuz, trade rerouting and increased ship-to-ship transfers since the conflict began in late February.
These disruptions have lengthened delivery times and reduced fleet efficiency, pushing freight rates higher.
As of the latest reports available up to Oct 22, VLCC tanker rates on key Middle East-to-Asia routes have reached  US$1 million to US$1.4 million a day, although some routes have eased from their peaks.
At a daily equivalent rate of US$1.4 million, a 30-day round voyage would imply about US$42 million in time-charter-equivalent earnings.
Revenue Gains, Cost Pressures
Economists noted that the impact on Malaysia would be mixed, with higher crude prices potentially boosting petroleum revenue and encouraging exploration and production (E&P) activities.
Rising transportation and insurance costs could squeeze refining margins, increase fuel subsidy requirements and raise business operating costs.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said higher fuel and insurance costs were pushing up transportation expenses, requiring O&G companies to strengthen cost management and improve productivity.
"The O&G industry would need to be vigilant in managing their operating costs by ensuring operational excellence as their main tools to manage costs, along with increasing the productivity level," he told Business Times.
Afzanizam said oil transportation costs could rise further if the conflict persisted.
He added that disruptions to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz could increase the need for E&P activities as energy security risks remained elevated.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the impact of higher freight rates would vary across the O&G value chain.
"The impact is mixed. Higher freight costs will squeeze refining margins and increase crude import costs, while tanker operators such as MISC Bhd could benefit from stronger charter rates.
"Upstream producers should remain relatively insulated," he said.
Thong said further disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with higher insurance premiums and vessel shortages, could push freight rates higher.
However, he noted that rates were already exceptionally high and could retreat sharply if geopolitical tensions eased.
"Higher crude prices should benefit upstream producers and potentially increase government petroleum revenue.
"However, Malaysia is also a net importer of crude oil, meaning higher freight and energy costs could pressure refiners, increase subsidy requirements and raise business operating costs," he said.
Thong said the benefits would therefore be concentrated in upstream production and shipping, while the wider economy faced higher cost pressures.
Transport Cost Spike Seen Temporary
LBB International chief executive officer Dr Marco Tieman expects the impact on Malaysia's transportation costs to be temporary, despite the prospect of further escalation in the Middle East.
"The situation is a little bit fluid with an increasing escalation in the Middle East expected in the coming weeks.
"I don't think this will be long term impact to the transportation costs for Malaysia," he said.
Tieman added that Malaysia is in a favourable position as a significant O&G producer.
Nevertheless, the IEA has noted that the disruption extended beyond crude oil shipments, affecting the availability of vessels used to transport refined petroleum products.
The agency said exceptionally high earnings from crude shipping had encouraged some tanker owners to redeploy Long Range 2 (LR2) vessels, which are commonly used for long-haul oil product shipments, to carry crude instead.
This has reduced vessel availability in the oil product tanker market, pushing up freight rates as cargoes are redistributed among smaller vessels.
By mid-October, freight rates for Long Range 1 (LR1) tankers travelling from the Persian Gulf to Japan had climbed to nearly US$27 per barrel, about five times their pre-conflict levels, the IEA said.
The agency also reported that shipping costs had risen sharply on other routes, with rates for Suezmax tankers carrying crude from West Africa to Europe exceeding US$22 per barrel by mid-October, more than four times their pre-conflict levels.

Title: 16 areas record unhealthy API readings, Johan Setia highest at 161
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johan Setia recorded the highest unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 161, with 15 other areas also logging unhealthy air quality as of 8am today.
Checks on the DOE's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Klang in Selangor at 159, followed by Nilai and Seremban in Negri Sembilan at 158 each.
Batu Muda and Petaling Jaya recorded readings of 157, followed by Shah Alam at 155, Banting at 153 and Putrajaya at 152.
Melaka's Bukit Rambai and Batu Pahat in Johor recorded readings of 151, while Tangkak recorded 141. Bandaraya Melaka and Alor Gajah recorded readings of 126 and 116, respectively.
In Sarawak, Sri Aman recorded an unhealthy reading of 151.
Meanwhile, 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, with Port Dickson in Negri Sembilan recording the highest at 99, followed by Kluang, Johor at 97 and IPD Serian, Sarawak at 93.
Rompin in Pahang recorded a reading of 84, followed by Temerloh at 78 and Jerantut at 77.
Terengganu's Paka recorded 78, while Kuala Terengganu and Besut recorded 57 and 56 respectively.
In Kelantan, Tanah Merah and Kota Baru recorded readings of 75 and 63, respectively.
Up north, Seri Manjung recorded the highest reading in Perak at 83, followed by Tasek Ipoh at 82, Tanjung Malim at 81, Pegoh Ipoh at 71 and Taiping at 66.
In Penang, Seberang Perai recorded 72, followed by Seberang Jaya at 63, and Minden and Balik Pulau at 62 each.
Kangar in Perlis recorded 61, while Sungai Petani, Kulim Hi-Tech, Alor Star and Langkawi in Kedah recorded readings of 59, 57, 56 and 53 respectively.
In Johor, Segamat recorded 87, Pasir Gudang 82, Larkin 80, Pengerang 72 and Kota Tinggi 65.
In Selangor, Kuala Selangor recorded a moderate reading of 75.
In Sarawak, Sibu and Samarahan recorded 85 each, followed by Sarikei at 73, Bintulu at 72, Samalaju, Kapit and Kuching at 71 each, Mukah at 65, Miri at 61 and Limbang at 59. ILP Miri recorded 57.
In Sabah, Tawau recorded 80, Keningau 78, Kota Kinabalu 59, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu 58, and Sandakan 56. Labuan recorded a reading of 72.
Only two areas nationwide recorded good API readings, with Kimanis in Sabah recording 48 and Kemaman in Terengganu 47.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: The ones who get it done
Article:
WHY do bosses repeatedly turn to certain members of staff when there is a job to be done?
Why do some employees seem to carry a heavier burden than others, often becoming the first people approached when deadlines loom, problems arise or expectations are not being met?
The answer lies in a combination of trust, competence, reliability and attitude.
In every workplace, there are people who do more than simply fulfil the requirements of their job. They make things happen.
Their value is not always reflected in their job title, salary or position on the organisational chart, but it becomes unmistakable when something important needs to be accomplished.
These employees have earned something that cannot easily be demanded or manufactured: confidence in their ability to deliver.
When a boss assigns a task, there is always an element of risk. Will it be completed on time? Will the quality be acceptable? Will someone need to be constantly reminded, supervised or rescued along the way?
Employees who consistently deliver reduce that uncertainty. A manager can hand them a responsibility and concentrate on other matters, knowing that the work is likely to be completed without unnecessary drama.
Reliability, therefore, is a valuable workplace currency. It is built through repeated actions, not grand promises.
People who keep their word, meet deadlines, communicate honestly and take responsibility for their mistakes gradually become the people others depend on.
Another important quality is the ability to find solutions rather than merely identify problems. Every workplace encounters obstacles, misunderstandings and unexpected setbacks.
Some employees wait for instructions whenever something goes wrong. Others assess the situation, consider the options and suggest a practical way forward.
This does not mean that valuable employees must have every answer. It means they are willing to think, exercise judgement and make a constructive contribution.
They understand that the objective is not simply to explain why something cannot be done, but to explore how it might be achieved.
Initiative also sets these employees apart. They do not always wait to be asked before noticing what needs attention.
They anticipate difficulties, recognise opportunities for improvement and act within the limits of their authority.
Their contribution extends beyond the immediate task because they understand the wider objective.
Equally important is their attitude towards responsibility. When a task becomes difficult, they do not immediately search for someone to blame.
They focus on what can be controlled, acknowledge their part in a problem and work towards a solution. This sense of ownership gives managers confidence that challenges will be addressed rather than quietly abandoned.
Communication is another defining characteristic. Employees who provide clear updates, raise concerns early and ask sensible questions make it easier for others to do their jobs.
They do not leave their managers guessing about progress or conceal problems until it is too late to resolve them. Good communication builds trust because it replaces uncertainty with information.
There is also the question of emotional maturity. Workplaces involve different personalities, competing priorities and occasional tension.
People who remain composed under pressure, accept feedback without becoming defensive and disagree respectfully are often particularly valuable.
They help maintain momentum when circumstances become stressful, rather than adding another problem for everyone else to manage.
These qualities explain why certain employees are repeatedly chosen for important assignments. However, there is a less comfortable side to this pattern. Being dependable can become a burden.
Once a manager discovers who can be trusted to deliver, it is tempting to keep returning to the same person, even when others could reasonably share the responsibility.
What begins as recognition can gradually become overreliance. The capable employee receives more work, more urgent requests and more difficult assignments, while colleagues with less initiative may escape the same level of scrutiny.
Eventually, competence is rewarded with an ever-growing workload rather than greater opportunity, recognition or support.
This is where good management matters. A capable employee should not become the permanent solution to every organisational problem.
Managers must distinguish between recognising someone's strengths and taking unfair advantage of their willingness to help.
Work should be distributed sensibly, expectations should be realistic, and exceptional contributions should be acknowledged.
It is also worth remembering that being repeatedly selected does not always mean an employee is the most talented person in the room.
Sometimes the decision reflects familiarity, convenience or a manager's preference for someone who works in a particular way.
Good leaders must remain alert to favouritism and ensure that quieter employees are not overlooked simply because they promote themselves less confidently.
For employees, the lesson is equally important. Being dependable is a strength, but it should not require unlimited availability or the silent acceptance of unreasonable demands.
The ability to set boundaries, communicate capacity and ask for support is part of professional maturity. Sustainable performance is more valuable than a short burst of extraordinary effort followed by exhaustion.
Ultimately, bosses turn to particular staff members because those employees offer something more meaningful than obedience.
They offer confidence. They combine competence with judgement, responsibility with initiative, and commitment with the ability to work constructively alongside others.
Their greatest value is not that they can be given more work than everyone else.
It is that they make difficult things easier, uncertain situations more manageable and shared objectives more achievable. They are the people who turn intentions into results.
But organisations must recognise a fundamental truth: the people who consistently get things done should not simply be given more to do.
They should be developed, respected, fairly rewarded and given opportunities to grow. Otherwise, the very qualities that make them valuable may eventually become the reasons they leave.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia records over 333,000 acute respiratory infection cases as fires rage
Article:
ISTANBUL: Indonesia has recorded 333,470 cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) linked to forest and land fires in several regions, the Health Ministry said on Thursday.
The ministry's director of environmental health, Then Suyanti, said daily cases remained high, with 4,522 new cases reported, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing state-run news agency Antara.
She said the latest Air Pollutant Index showed that air quality in several areas had reached hazardous levels, particularly in six provinces prioritised for fire management: Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, South Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan.
Suyanti said exposure to wildfire smoke, which contains fine particulate matter such as PM2.5, carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide and other organic compounds, can cause health problems, including ARIs, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, eye and skin irritation, and other systemic health effects.
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said on Thursday that if foreign-backed companies were responsible for recurring forest and land fires, they could lose their operating permits, and revoked concessions could be reassigned to younger Indonesians.
"Regarding forest fires, there are indications that many foreign companies bear responsibility. They have held concessions for over a decade, yet some have committed violations three, four, or even a dozen times — some as many as 19 times," Prabowo said, adding that their permits should be revoked if they committed two violations.
Separately, thousands of students and others demonstrated in Samarinda, the capital of East Kalimantan, demanding that the government declare forest and land fires a national disaster, according to iNews.
Indonesia is experiencing an unusually prolonged dry season, with El Niño contributing to conditions favourable for wildfires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: At least 16 dead in Tibet quake
Article:
BEIJING: At least 16 people were killed and 32 others injured when a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China's remote Tibet region, state news agency Xinhua reported, citing local authorities.
More than 300 houses collapsed in the earthquake, which struck on Thursday at 10.33pm (1433 GMT). Officials were still assessing the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, Xinhua said.
The quake's epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190km east-northeast of Nagqu and 390km northeast of the regional capital, Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.
It struck at a shallow depth of 10km.
A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said.
The epicentre was located in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in its walls, according to Xinhua.
Power and telecommunications services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.
Earthquakes are relatively common in China.
In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet's rural Tingri county.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New York votes to ban Central Park horse carriages after decades of debate
Article:
NEW YORK: New York's City Council on Thursday voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, signalling the end of a tourist ritual that has been the subject of heated debate for years.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who must sign the measure into law, had previously voiced support for such a ban but has also expressed concerns about protections for workers in the industry.
If the mayor signs it, the ban will take effect in June 2028.
The lead-up period is intended to help the approximately 150 active carriage drivers find new employment, City Council Speaker Julie Menin told journalists ahead of the vote.
The Transport Workers Union, which represents the workers, has vowed to take legal action.
Legislative battles over the fate of the cultural tradition, which is nearly as old as Central Park itself, have been ongoing for nearly two decades.
Critics say the animals suffer, pointing to deadly collapses and dangerous escapes, while advocates highlight the jobs they create and the heritage they uphold.
The bill includes a provision to explore potential compensation for licence holders, Menin said.
It mandates that owners of the nearly 200 horses would not be allowed to sell them for slaughter or to other horse-carriage businesses.
The rides — featured in film and television, including a scene with Robert Redford and Jane Fonda in "Barefoot in the Park" and a dramatic ride in "Sex and the City" — currently cost US$150 for 45 minutes, rising to several hundred dollars for a marriage proposal.
But after years of wrangling over the issue, the summer season proved decisive in sounding the death knell for the Manhattan carriages.
In June, an 18-year-old tourist from India was killed by a horse that broke loose and bolted.
That followed a series of other incidents involving the carriages, including the deaths of several horses.
The Central Park Conservancy, which manages the US's most frequented urban park, with 42 million annual visits, also threw its weight behind calls for a ban, saying it had become "a matter of public health and safety".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLIA emerges as key airport for smuggling young gibbons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Young gibbons are being hidden in suitcases and smuggled on passenger flights, with  Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) the most frequently implicated airport in a new study.
The wildlife trade monitoring organisation Traffic recorded at least 86 gibbons intercepted in 33 airport smuggling incidents linked to Southeast Asia between January 2024 and last August.
KLIA was linked to 16 cases involving at least 54 gibbons, including 32 seized at the airport.
The animals were concealed in pet carriers or plastic baskets inside checked-in luggage. Every gibbon whose life stage was known was an infant or juvenile, read the report.
Demand for exotic pets helps drive the trade, although investigators must establish whether particular shipments were intended for pet owners or captive facilities.
[[nid:1561704]]
Traffic Southeast Asia director Kanitha Krishnasamy warned that small shipments could cause devastating losses.
"The smuggling of just a few gibbons on each flight may seem small in isolation, but like a dripping tap, the losses accumulate over time.
"What appears minor  can add up to a devastating toll on wild populations," she said.
The report also documented seven gibbons found dead in May last year after reportedly being flown from Malaysia in suitcases.
Adults may be harmed or killed when young gibbons are captured, adding to losses beyond the animals seized.
At least 38 people were arrested in connection with the airport incidents. Some couriers were allegedly offered cash, flights and accommodation to transport wildlife.
Traffic warned that detected cases likely underestimated the trade's true scale and called for stronger airport screening and investigations targeting trafficking networks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of weakening Typhoon Champi, hundreds of flights cancelled
Article:
TAIPEI: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, although the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.
At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191kph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).
The storm was about 330km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. Its forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north towards the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.
The administration said its radius was around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.
Taiwan's financial markets will also close on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which lie next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal.
The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights scheduled for Friday had been cancelled, along with more than 350 international flights.
Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, helping to keep casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn, bringing strong winds and torrential rain.
The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US judge orders Trump to testify in BBC defamation case by Dec 11
Article:
MIAMI: A US judge on Thursday set a Dec 11 deadline for President Donald Trump to testify under oath in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC.
Judge Enjolique Lett in Miami issued the order in response to complaints by the British broadcaster that Trump had refused to sit for a deposition, including cancelling a previously agreed date of Oct 16.
If Trump fails to attend the deposition by the deadline, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said.
Trump has accused the BBC of deceptively editing its documentary "Trump: A Second Chance" to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the US Capitol on Jan 6, 2021, after losing the presidential election.
The crowd proceeded to storm Congress in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden's victory.
While the BBC has apologised for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, the broadcaster has denied causing Trump any real injury and has sought to have the case dismissed.
Trump filed his lawsuit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least US$5 billion on each of two counts.
Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, told the court that Trump had no real excuse for not testifying and that on Oct 16, he had only been campaigning, "participating in party politics".
"No plaintiff is above the law," Tobin said.
In a court filing on Wednesday, Trump's legal team argued that he was not seeking to avoid a deposition but had been constrained by "matters of national importance".
The lawyers said Trump would be able to give a deposition between Jan 11 and 22.
Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters who ask questions he does not like and seeking to bar outlets airing critical reports from the White House.
Most recently, the administration has become embroiled in a legal dispute with CNN, MSNOW and Politico over attempts to bar them from the White House.
With his approval ratings in the low 30 per cent range and polls showing his Republican Party likely to lose control of the House of Representatives in the Nov 3 midterm elections, Trump faces increasing headwinds as he approaches his final years in power.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NUTP: Teachers lack training to detect violent behaviour among students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Teachers are not trained to spot or handle aggressive and extremist behaviour among schoolchildren, as they can only rely on the discipline guidebook to address issues, said the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP).
NUTP secretary-general Fouzi Singon said current school guidelines do not equip teachers with the skills needed to manage  cases of such behaviour.
"Even discipline teachers or student affairs assistants do not get specific training on the matter. All that is available is a general briefing on the discipline rulebook or circulars," he told
New Straits Times
.
He said without proper training, teachers cannot distinguish violent behaviours and must rely on their own experience.
"A teacher simply reports the case to the principal or senior assistant for action like calling the parents or expelling the student."
Last week, Public Accounts Committee chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin raised concerns about nihilistic violent extremism (NVE) among school-children, which requires joint action by the government, schools and parents.
NVE is an emerging form of extremism involving violence without a clear political, religious or conventional ideological agenda.
On Wednesday, a male student, 16, allegedly  brought firecrackers and an axe to an international school, injuring a female teacher.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said  Kuching  police received information on the incident at 8.03am.
"The victim reportedly sustained a cut to her hand," he said.
Fouzi urged the Education Ministry  to involve ground-level educators when devising new school safety policies.
"NUTP must be involved in drafting any policy so that teachers' real experiences on the ground can serve as a guide."
Parent Action Group for Education said parents and educational institutions must take proactive steps to address warning signs in children rather than waiting for violent incidents to occur.
Chairman Datin Noor Azimah Abdul Rahim said early action was key to keeping students safe.
"The priority is to identify risks early, intervene proportionately and ensure that every child has a safe route to seek help without fear of being condemned or abandoned," she said, adding that trust was vital because children, who fear punishment or humiliation, might hide their  experiences.
"Parental responsibility cannot stop at simply asking children whether they are safe online. Where there are credible warning signs, parents may need to take more active protective steps."
She said schools needed accessible pathways to trained mental health professionals, child protection services and law enforcement when warranted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump to move forward with planned arch project despite legal action
Article:
WASHINGTON: Construction of a massive arch in Washington proposed by US President Donald Trump could move ahead despite ongoing legal action, with a recent court filing saying work could begin in two weeks.
The proposed giant structure along the Potomac River near Arlington National Cemetery is part of Trump's drive to put his personal stamp on the US capital.
In a court filing on Wednesday, the Trump administration said "construction could commence as early as November 5", the same day a commission aligned with Trump is scheduled to vote on approving the project's proposed site and building plans.
The planned 76-metre triumphal white arch — dwarfing the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, which inspired it — would also feature gold statues of an angel and eagles at the top.
The project's height would interrupt sightlines between the Lincoln Memorial, one of Washington's iconic landmarks, and Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place of hundreds of thousands of American service members.
In September, US District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered the Trump administration to "provide the court with 48 hours' notice before engaging in any activity" on the site "related to or in preparation for the construction of an arch".
The lawsuit against the project was filed in February by Vietnam War veterans, who argued that such a massive undertaking requires approval by Congress.
Since returning to office in 2025, Trump, a former real estate mogul, has launched a series of renovation projects, several of which have prompted legal disputes.
They include a massive, costly ballroom being built at the White House, for which Trump had an entire wing of the presidential mansion demolished, and the Kennedy Center performance venue, which the president threatened to demolish unless his name was displayed on it.
The latest case involves the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic golf course Trump wants to redesign but where the project has faced legal setbacks after hundreds of trees were cut down.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Starshield system is 'back' in Ukraine: Trump
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Starshield military communications system is "back" in Ukraine, Donald Trump said on Thursday, after The Wall Street Journal reported that the US president had asked tech billionaire Elon Musk to restore the service, which is vital to Kyiv's forces.
"I don't want to comment on it, you know, whether I called or whether somebody else called — doesn't make any difference," Trump told journalists when asked about the report.
"I guess the bottom line, he put it back," Trump said, referring to Musk.
The Journal reported earlier this week that Musk had capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, rendering some of Kyiv's drones useless.
Musk had previously said that "any limits on speed or usage" of Starshield systems — operated by his SpaceX company — were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS", referring to Trump.
But Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday that the Pentagon had not directed any changes to Starshield, and Trump said last week that he had not done so either.
Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink's military-grade satellite service, for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and its interceptor drones. It also uses SpaceX's parallel civilian satellite system, Starlink.
Relations between Washington and Kyiv have been increasingly tense in recent days, with Trump calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to be replaced after he criticised a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says wind turbine imports threaten national security
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday declared imports of wind turbines and their components a threat to national security, but stopped short of imposing new tariffs on the sector.
In a White House proclamation, Trump said a Commerce Department investigation found that imported wind turbines threatened national security because of cybersecurity concerns linked to foreign-made equipment, interference with radar systems and air traffic operations, and increased US reliance on goods made overseas.
The move follows a probe launched in August 2025 under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act. It is one of numerous trade investigations the administration has conducted into the national security implications of imports across a range of sectors.
Instead of imposing immediate trade restrictions, Trump directed trade officials to pursue negotiations with trading partners and report back within 180 days.
Additional trade measures, including tariffs, could be considered later, the order said.
The order reiterates Trump's longstanding criticism of wind energy as unreliable because of its intermittent nature.
"Given wind energy's intermittent reliability, use of wind energy diverts the United States electrical grid from more reliable energy sources," the order said.
Major suppliers of wind turbines and components to the US include Mexico, France, India, Denmark and Germany, according to trade data cited by the centre-right think tank American Action Forum.
A spokesperson for the American Clean Power Association, a trade group representing clean energy companies, was not immediately available for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Around 150,000 rally in Belgrade as Serbia heads to pivotal poll
Article:
BELGRADE: Around 150,000 supporters of Serbia's opposition student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday, seeking to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic in a pivotal parliamentary election this weekend.
The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, wants to end more than 14 years of rule by Vucic's right-wing populist Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in Sunday's vote.
It poses the biggest threat Vucic has faced, and civil society groups have warned that the election campaign has been marred by intimidation, arrests, attacks, misuse of public resources and a distorted media environment.
"I came to support the Student List because young people finally gave me hope that it is possible to live in a normal country," 47-year-old Marija Nedeljkovic Radic told AFP as she arrived for the rally.
"Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible."
Around 150,000 people gathered at the Student List rally in Belgrade on Thursday evening, according to the independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings in a post on X.
The vote comes after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated Novi Sad railway station, which killed 16 people.
The tragedy, widely blamed on corruption, triggered some of Serbia's largest protests since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.
The anti-corruption movement, led by university students, grew from demands for a transparent investigation into the tragedy into calls for an early election.
Waving "Students are winning" flags, chanting and blowing whistles, students and their supporters marched through Belgrade before converging on Slavija Square, the site of some of their biggest protests.
They filled the square and surrounding streets, according to AFP reporters.
"We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours," university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of 250 candidates on the Student List, told the crowd, which chanted "Victory, victory!"
"You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!"
The rally ended with the candidates stepping down from the stage into the crowd, holding the Serbian constitution and dancing a traditional folk dance with supporters.
[[nid:1561671]]
Vucic defiant
Vucic has dominated Serbian politics for more than a decade, serving as either prime minister or president.
Amid mounting pressure, Vucic announced the snap election last month, setting up his biggest electoral challenge since his party took power in 2012.
Vucic, who addressed supporters at a sports hall in the capital on Thursday, has regularly accused the student movement of being a foreign-funded coup attempt.
"Let us never forget how they tried to bring down our state. Let us always protect and defend it," said the 56-year-old, who resigned to run for prime minister.
"Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!" he said before white ticker tape and balloons showered the crowd.
Many of the 250 candidates on the Student List running for the 250-seat parliament are drawn from academia or are deliberate political outsiders.
The movement has a broad platform, but its core pledge is to fight corruption.
Serbia lacks reliable independent polling, and surveys have produced widely differing results.
Political scientist Dusan Vucicevic of Belgrade University told AFP it was difficult to predict the outcome but expected the students to win more than 40 per cent of the vote, a result significantly higher than that of any opposition list since the SNS came to power.
Threats, intimidation
Days before the vote, Serbian civil society groups warned that conditions for "free and fair elections" were lacking.
"This assessment is not based on isolated incidents, opposition claims or political disagreement with the government," a joint statement by 24 organisations said.
"It is supported by documented findings from independent Serbian organisations working in different fields."
On Wednesday, Belgrade prosecutors questioned six people arrested on suspicion of plotting "violence, riots and attacks" on election day.
Reports of threats and intimidation targeting student demonstrators have grown in recent months, but their rallies have remained largely peaceful since they began.
"I've been following this fight since the very beginning," 35-year-old rally attendee Igor said.
"Today is the last rally, and it's important that we all come here to send a message of love and peace and that we see each other on the 25th at the polling stations."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deadly fire at Canada military base was caused by live grenade exercise
Article:
OTTAWA: A fast-moving grass fire that killed at least four soldiers at a  western Canadian military base on Saturday was sparked by an exercise using live grenades, a senior defence official said on Thursday.
High winds then propelled the blaze across the army base in Wainwright, overwhelming dozens of soldiers. The incident was one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military.
"The fire initiated on the automatic grenade launcher range ... (it) initiated as a result of routine military training that was happening on that range at the time," Brigadier-General Vanessa Hanrahan told reporters.
Officials said 27 people remain hospitalised, several in critical condition. The soldiers and reserve members were preparing to deploy to Latvia, where Canadian forces have their largest international military operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian police link 11 firms to forest, land fires
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Police have named 11 corporations as suspects in ongoing investigations into forest and land fires, three of which are foreign-invested firms, according to the Antara news agency.
National police chief General Suyudi Ario Seto declined to name the companies but said the investigations were proceeding without major obstacles.
He told reporters following a plenary Cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace complex here on Wednesday that accountability would extend beyond the corporate entities.
"This includes both company owners and shareholders who bear responsibility for the corporations linked to forest and land fires in Indonesia," said Suyudi.
The report said the criminal proceedings followed an earlier announcement by the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency, which said it had raised 98 police reports concerning corporate-linked forest fires to the formal investigation stage.
Alongside the police investigations, the Forestry Ministry has stepped up administrative enforcement.
Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said permits for six more companies in Central Kalimantan had been suspended, bringing the total number of forestry firms sanctioned to 32, according to the report.
The six companies had their Forest Utilisation Business Permits suspended and were ordered to undertake environmental restoration in affected areas.
Together, they hold concessions covering 201,391ha, of which 7,531ha were affected by recent fires.
The ministry's administrative sanctions now cover 32 companies managing more than 1.9 million hectares of concessions, including 18,489ha affected by fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOfinance tops 5m users, processes RM3.57b
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: TNG Digital Sdn Bhd's GOfinance platform has recorded more than five million distinct investment users and processed RM3.57 billion in investment value as of Sept 30.
The financial services hub, available through TNG eWallet, offers a range of investment products, including money market funds, Amanah Saham, unit trusts, retirement solutions, digital gold and shares in local and overseas markets.
Selected products allow users to start investing with as little as RM10 and explore options that match their financial goals and risk appetite.
TNG Digital chief financial services officer Desmond Teoh said accessibility meant more than lowering minimum investment amounts; users also needed convenient access to a range of investment options.
"We recognise that trust matters when people make decisions about their money. Our aim is to give users a practical starting point and access to options as their financial needs change," he said.
The company said more than 4.7 million users had invested in GO+, while over 700,000 had traded digital gold through e-Mas.
TNG Digital said the figure represented unique users, with each user counted only once even if they had accessed multiple wealth products.
The company operates an open-platform model that connects its user base with established, regulated financial institutions and specialist partners to broaden access to investment products.
TNG Digital's partnerships have expanded the investment options available through TNG eWallet. Its collaboration with Webull, announced on Sept 30, introduced access to global share trading.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Public can check 5-day air quality forecasts via MyCMAQ
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Malaysians can use the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (MyCMAQ) to check air pollution forecasts up to five days ahead.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the system, developed by the Meteorological Department, provided high-resolution forecasts of air quality and atmospheric pollutant concentrations in Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia.
"I hope the public will refer to this platform so they can make preparations and take the necessary action for activities over the next five days," he said during Ministers' Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
He was responding to Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong), who asked about measures taken to ensure accurate and timely air quality information amid the current haze situation.
Arthur said the system was designed to provide more responsive air quality forecasts and haze warnings that were easier for the public to understand.
He added that the 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment monitored six major air pollutants continuously.
"These stations use measurement equipment based on technical methods and standards recognised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency to ensure the accuracy and reliability of their readings."
Arthur said the government understood that some areas did not have dedicated monitoring stations.
"In such cases, data from the nearest monitoring station will be used."
He added that the ministry would increase the number of monitoring stations to obtain more accurate readings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt coordinating efforts to address mental health issues, says Dzulkefly
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Pressure to achieve academic and career success, relationship problems, social media influence and financial difficulties are among the main factors affecting young people's mental health.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) found that 4.6 per cent of Malaysians aged 16 and above, or about one million people, suffered from depression.
Young people recorded the highest prevalence, at 7.9 per cent among those aged 16 to 19, and 7.6 per cent among those aged 20 to 29.
In a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (Pas-Tumpat), who asked about the mental well-being of young people, Dzulkefly said his ministry had established the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health to coordinate government policies and initiatives on mental health.
The centre is responsible for addressing mental health crises, developing policies, implementing interventions and providing training.
Dzulkefly said the ministry also welcomed a proposal to establish an interministerial task force to pool expertise and strengthen early intervention.
Several cross-ministry initiatives were already in place, he said, including the  Healthy Minds Programme with the Education Ministry and the Healthy Student Programme with the Higher Education Ministry.
He said the ministry also served as a referral centre for cases requiring further assessment through KafeTeen services under the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry.
Meanwhile, the 2022 NHMS, which assessed post-partum depression, found that 11.2 per cent of mothers experienced the condition, with nine in 10 unaware they had it.
Dzulkefly said post-partum depression was more prevalent among younger mothers and those living in urban areas.
He said families, friends and the wider community had a role in recognising signs of mental health issues among young people for early intervention and treatment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump ordered to testify under oath in US$10bil BBC lawsuit
Article:
WASHINGTON: A federal judge on Thursday ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by Dec 11 in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath, the Associated Press reported.
Trump is suing Britain's publicly funded broadcaster for at least US$10 billion over a misleadingly edited clip of a speech. The case is one of several Trump has privately filed against the news media as part of wider pressure campaign against coverage he dislikes.
US Magistrate Judge Enjolique Lett ordered Trump to take questions from the BBC's lawyers under oath in a ruling from the bench at a court hearing on Thursday, according to the AP. Trump canceled a deposition in October, citing conflicts with his presidential duties.
Representatives for Trump's legal team and the BBC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Trump's lawsuit filed in December in Florida federal court accuses the BBC of intentionally misleading viewers into thinking he directed supporters to storm the US Capitol by splicing together different parts of a Jan 6, 2021 speech.
The BBC admitted the edits were misleading and apologised to Trump, though it denies being liable for defamation.
In court filings, the broadcaster has accused Trump and his lawyers of dragging their feet in response to their requests for records and other information that is exchanged between parties in a process known as discovery.
The BBC is seeking financial records from Trump's Mar-a-Lago club and the web of business entities associated with him, saying the information is necessary to defend against Trump's damages claims.
Trump's lawyers say the requests are too broad and irrelevant to the case. They have also denied in court filings that Trump is avoiding a deposition, saying Trump's duties and security needs must take precedence.
The edited speech appeared in a BBC "Panorama" documentary show shortly before the 2024 presidential election, which Trump won. A leaked internal BBC memo cited the edits as evidence of potential political bias, sparking a public relations crisis for the broadcaster and leading to high-level resignations.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka election: Rauf appointed BN's election director
Article:
AYER KEROH: Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has been appointed the coalition's election director for the upcoming state polls.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, in announcing this, said this was because the coalition's election director, deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was busy with his duties as foreign minister.
"Before this it was Tok Mat (Mohamad) but as foreign minister, he is rather busy. By coincidence, while the campaigning for the Melaka election is ongoing, (Mohamad) will be overseas, including attending a meeting of the Commonwealth nations and the Asean Summit in Manila.
"So, I proposed (that Rauf takes over as BN's Melaka election director) and the meeting earlier endorsed this... no one else, just him (Rauf)," he said after chairing the BN central committee meeting for the 16th Melaka election.
Meanwhile, Rauf, who is also Melaka caretaker chief minister, said he appreciated the trust placed on him to be the election director.
He said he and the party's leadership team would fulfil their responsibilities to the best of their ability.
"At the meeting earlier, we reached agreement on many matters, including coordinating the duties and responsibilities of 'mentors' and BN component parties in supporting election campaign efforts in Melaka.
"I hope this mutual understanding will provide us with a good opportunity to achieve our goal of ensuring that this Melaka election reflects a united front through collective cooperation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen, 13, allegedly knifes 69-year-old man in Kanowit public toilet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — A 69-year-old man was injured in the shoulder after he was allegedly attacked with a knife by a 13-year-old boy at a public toilet in Kanowit, Sarawak, yesterday.
Sinar Harian
reported Kanowit district police chief DSP Junical Ujal as saying police received a report of the incident at 3.29pm.
“According to the call, a 13-year-old boy was reported to have injured a man using a knife.
“The victim is now receiving treatment at Kanowit Hospital and is reported to have suffered minor injuries to his left shoulder,” he was quoted as saying in a statement.
Junical said the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
He said police are conducting a thorough investigation to establish the full cause of the incident and gather related evidence.
He also urged the public not to speculate or spread unverified information about the case, out of respect for the investigation process and the interests of all parties involved.
Earlier, a claim went viral on social media alleging that a toilet attendant had been attacked by a teenage boy with a sharp object at a public toilet in the district.

Title: Anwar vows Malaysia’s support for peace and stability in southern Thailand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysia is committed to playing a constructive role in supporting efforts to achieve regional peace and stability, including in southern Thailand, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said dialogue based on trust, mutual understanding and openness was crucial to paving the way for a comprehensive and lasting peaceful solution for the wellbeing of the people in southern Thailand.
Anwar said this in a Facebook post last night after receiving a courtesy call from Malaysia’s Facilitator for the Southern Thailand Peace Dialogue Process, Lt Gen (Rtd) Datuk Ahmad Norihan Jalal, who was recently appointed to the post. — Bernama

Title: Taiping council denies Osaka zoo elephants abused, says head swaying and musth normal in captivity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Taiping Municipal Council (MPT) has rejected claims that the three Malaysian elephants sent to Japan’s Tennoji Zoo in Osaka are being abused or neglected, insisting the animals are healthy and have settled into their new surroundings.
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT)
reported MPT president Mohamed Akmal Dahalan as saying that Dara, Amoi and Kelat were reunited on September 20 after being kept apart for a period following their transfer, and now have free access to the whole enclosure.
He was responding to concerns raised on social media that the elephants were displaying behaviour such as head swaying, zoochosis and frequent musth episodes.
Mohamed Akmal said in a statement that such behaviour could not be directly attributed to stress, depression or neglect.
“Head swaying is also a typical behaviour when elephants anticipate food. On the other hand, the frequent episodes of musth experienced by Kelat is caused by the animal being fed highly nutritious food.
“Both behaviours are normal for elephants put under the care of zoos,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that Tennoji Zoo is running enrichment programmes to safeguard the animals’ wellbeing.
The elephants were sent to Osaka in March under a 25-year cooperation agreement between Taiping Zoo & Night Safari and Tennoji Zoo, a move that has drawn criticism from animal welfare groups and members of the public.
MPT has consistently maintained that the arrangement is a non-commercial, zoo-to-zoo programme and that the elephants remain the property of Taiping Zoo.

Title: 1MDB debt in 2026: RM42.5b paid, but RM20.1b still remains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The remaining net financial burden borne by the government in relation to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) is estimated at RM20.1 billion, assuming no further recovery of funds or assets in the future.
According to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), this figure accounts for the government’s total financial obligations related to 1MDB — amounting to RM51.4 billion — after deducting recovered funds and assets totalling RM31.3 billion.
“Since the government began assuming the debt obligations and financial commitments related to 1MDB in April 2017, it has settled payments totalling RM42.5 billion, comprising RM27.7 billion in principal payments, and RM14.8 billion in interest and other commitments,” the MOF said in a written reply on the Parliament website yesterday to a question from Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor) regarding new mechanisms to ensure that liabilities similar to those of 1MDB are not shifted onto taxpayers, as well as assurances that the claims process will not be compromised by developments concerning the criminal sentencing of the perpetrators.
The ministry said the outstanding commitment for government-guaranteed Islamic medium-term notes (IMTN) amounts to RM8.9 billion, comprising RM5 billion in principal and RM3.9 billion in interest, lasting until the maturity date in 2039.
Regarding efforts to recover funds, the MOF affirmed that the government remains committed to pursuing claims and asset recovery efforts related to 1MDB.
“Any developments concerning criminal sentencing or the granting of a pardon to an individual do not, in themselves, terminate civil claims aimed at recovering misappropriated funds.
“Civil claims have a different basis of action and evidentiary process compared to criminal proceedings,” the ministry said.
The MOF noted that, consequently, the implications of any decision regarding sentencing or a pardon under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution must be examined based on the scope of that decision and the applicable laws.
“The right of the government and 1MDB to pursue civil claims should be assessed based on the grounds for the claims, the evidence, and the court orders within those proceedings; meanwhile, any asset forfeiture action is subject to the legal provisions and conditions that govern such measures.
“The government’s stance is firm: efforts to recover state funds will continue through available legal channels, while respecting the jurisdiction of the courts and the power of pardon as provided for under the Federal Constitution,” the ministry said.
The MOF noted that the government’s priority is to maximise the recovery of funds to settle 1MDB’s obligations, reduce the nation’s financial burden, and safeguard the interests of the people. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina: Budget 2027 to drive new curriculum and Malaysia Education Plan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) will focus on rolling out the new curriculum and the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035 next year, using the 2027 Budget allocation to drive improvements in the quality of education.
Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the main challenge was ensuring the ministry could implement announced plans and initiatives effectively in the interests of students and educators.
“This allocation enables us to implement the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035, particularly next year’s key focus, the new curriculum.
“Indeed, this budget clearly prioritises the quality of education,” she said after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme, “Belanjawan 2027: Memperkukuh Pendidikan, Melakar Masa Depan,” at Wisma Bernama yesterday.
Fadhlina said the 2027 Budget also prioritised easing schooling costs for families through various aid and allowances, including the Form Six allowance, Early Schooling Aid (BAP), the allowance for Students with Special Educational Needs and incentives for special education teachers.
She added that special attention would also be given to development aspects, such as building new schools, upgrading dilapidated schools and school sports facilities.
Meanwhile, when asked about safety measures and improvements to standard operating procedures to address bullying in schools, Fadhlina stressed that the MOE takes a holistic and consistent approach, including empowering students.
“Among the measures we are consistently taking are conducting safety audits of dormitories, installing additional CCTV cameras, and providing warden assistants, which are crucial for student control and safety,” she said.
She said guidance and counselling teachers are also being trained to identify early signs of bullying, and that avenues for students to voice their views directly are being expanded.
“Schools belong to the community. So the community also has a responsibility to work together with us,” she said.
Earlier in the programme, Fadhlina said multi-storey construction methods and the modular Industrialised Building System would be a game changer in speeding up solutions for overcrowded and dilapidated schools.
Beyond physical aspects, she stressed that student welfare, particularly for those with special needs and children from low-income (B40) families, remained a key priority.
“The BAP must be understood in context: the allocation goes to all students regardless of background so that no child is left behind.
“The increase in the BAP rate from RM150 to RM200 per student is certainly a reason for gratitude, as it eases the financial burden on many families,” she said.
Fadhlina said the ministry is strengthening schools to prepare for climate change, including heatwaves and floods, through infrastructure and facility improvements.
“Ahead of the El Niño phenomenon, expected to bring hot weather throughout next year, the ministry and the secretary-general have discussed measures to create a more conducive learning environment,” she said.
Fadhlina said the ministry is also examining whether schools at risk of repeated flooding, particularly those near rivers and in valleys, need to be relocated or upgraded. — Bernama

Title: Penang hit-and-run: SUV driver arrested after killing two on expressway
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 23 — The driver suspected of being involved in a hit-and-run accident that killed two people on the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway near the Penang Bridge interchange yesterday morning has been arrested.
Timur Laut police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the 23-year-old man, who was driving a sport utility vehicle (SUV), was arrested at 1 pm after turning himself in at the Timur Laut District Police Headquarters (IPD) here.
"The man is from Bukit Jambul. A urine screening test conducted on the suspect found no drugs,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Abdul Rozak said police would apply for a remand order today to facilitate further investigations.
The victims, a 22-year-old man and his 20-year-old female pillion rider, were travelling from central George Town towards the Penang Bridge at about 4 am when the accident occurred.
Upon reaching the fork leading to the Penang Bridge and Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), their motorcycle was believed to have been hit from behind by a vehicle, killing both at the scene.
Abdul Rozak said post-mortem examinations found that the male motorcyclist died from severe head and neck injuries, while the woman died from severe head injuries.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Show me the money: A guide to getting the most out of your Budget 2027 financial aid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Budget 2027 is officially out, bringing a much-needed financial lifeline to Malaysians feeling the pinch of rising living costs.
Whether you are a gig worker looking to buy your first home, a parent managing back-to-school expenses, or a B40 household needing a monthly cash boost, the latest national budget packs targeted relief for almost everyone.
Here is your complete guide to the assistance schemes you can tap into next year.
Direct cash transfers: STR and SARA payouts
The Rahmah initiatives remain the foundation of the government’s welfare strategy, channelling direct support to lower-income households.
Under Budget 2027, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) provides up to RM150 a month, capping at RM1,800 annually for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients.
Adult Malaysians missing out on STR will also not walk away empty-handed. They will receive a total of RM200 through two RM100 SARA Madani payouts.
STR recipients (Monthly SARA)
Who qualifies:
Approved STR recipients.
Amount:
Up to RM150 a month, totalling RM1,800 a year.
How to use:
The government credits the funds directly to your MyKad. You can spend this at participating shops, supermarkets, and FAMA farmers’ markets to buy approved daily necessities.
How to apply:
Verify your status or update your details via the official MySTR portal.
Non-STR recipients (SARA Madani)
Who qualifies:
Malaysian citizens aged 18 and above who do not receive STR.
Amount:
